Mercedes

By: Tarryn Crossman | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
A doctored form of ecstacy that has put over 60 young people in hospital and killed 11

Summary:
Mercedes first made headlines in early March when 36 young people landed in hospital and 7 passed away after taking the drug, all over one weekend in Kwamashu, KZN
Sibongile was out with 4 friends, they bought 2 mercedes pills each and went to the local night club in the area. As recollected by his friends: Sibongile started to feel faint, he complained of burning up and went outside to get some air. They went to look for him and found him lying on the pavement. They rushed him to the nearest clinic where he was declared dead.
He was 19 years old.
His two friends can describe what the drug did to them and the experience of losing their best friend on the street outside a party. Their story makes the situation real

And then over the Easter weekend 23 kids landed in hospital and 4 died in Pietermaritzburg, after taking the drug.
It is a cheap form of ecstacy that is being cut with something that puts so much pressure on the bodies internal organs they collapse.
A task force has been created in KZN to investigate the drug. Sergent Ngobese is the head of the task force and will be able to explain what is in the drug, where it is spreading to and what they are doing to try and stop it.

Press Release:


Mercedes - The Killer Drug
What was supposed to be a fun evening out for a group of teenagers resulted in tragedy when 19-year-old Siyabonga’s lifeless body was found on the pavement. The cause? A deadly, mystery drug known on the streets of KwaZulu-Natal as Mercedes. This altered form of ecstasy has since claimed the lives of almost a dozen teenagers and landed another 60 in hospital. While its origins remain unknown, it seems readily available across the province. Was this just a single bad batch of ecstasy, or is it a new drug with fatal consequences?


Script:


Time code CHARACTER / VISUAL
1 00:00 Claire Mawisa to camera. Establishing shot Claire: Anew drug with the street name called Mercedes first made headlines in later march when 44 teenagers were hospitalized and 4 died after trying it. While the SAPS were investigating why this drug is so fatal yet another 23 teenagers were hospitalized and 4 passed away over the Easter weekend.
2 00:21 Nightlife in KwaMashu. V/O V/O: Siyabonga Mngadi was on of the 10 teenagers that have died from taking Mercedes over the last 2 months in KwaZulu Natal
3 00:29 Zodwa Grandmother of Siyabonga Zodwa: Siyabonga was a child that always laughed, he loved people and he loved his family. I last saw him on Friday he was very happy because he knew he was going out with his friends.
4 00:47 Khanyi Mngadi who is Siyabonga's sister Khanyi: Siyabonga took a drug called Mercedes he took the whole pill, they say its nit safe to take the whole pill you must cut it in half and Siyabonga was saying that his heart was beating so fast like he couldn’t breathe. Siyabonga said we must take him out because its Hot and I also asked them when they took him outside was Siyabonga dead or was he still alive? They told me he was still alive.
5 01:22 V/O with the club scene V/O: After losing 10 teenagers and further hospitalizing 60 teenagers over a 2 month period. KwaZulu Natal put together a provincial task team headed up by Sargent Ngobese to investigate what it is that is making Mercedes so fatal?
6 01:37 Claire interviews Sergeant Ngobese Claire: What is Mercedes?
Ngobese: Mercedes is quite a new drug that has not been in the market for a long time. It has just been introduced but we have since taken the drug to the national laboratory it was analysed and classified to be illegal drugs.
Claire: So what is Mercedes made up of?
Ngobese: Its already an existing ecstasy why has chemical that has been added on top of the ecstasy which is called Katina
Claire: So I still don’t understand is this a bad batch of ecstasy or is it totally a new drug?
Ngobese: I wouldn’t say it’s a bad batch that is killing the young people. I would say it the Mercedes drug that is killing our young people.
Claire: And how do you know tat?
Ngobese: Because it did not take place in one isolated incident. We had an incident at KwaMashu where lost 4 lives at one go, now you go to Pietermaritzburg 120km away from KwaMashu separate group and people have been loosing their lives then across the freeway on the Northern side of this district we have lost a life at Sobantu so those are many incidents, which don’t talk to each other. I want to safely say it’s not just a bad batch but it is the drug itself.

7 02:56 V/O
V/O: At this point the SAPS task team does not know whether Mercedes is being manufactured locally or is it imported. But they do know it’s easily available in taverns, nightclubs and dealers in the areas that are affected. Contrary to what the SAPS is saying though one of Siyabonga’s friend who has taken Mercedes and being hospitalized after using it says this drug has been around a lot longer than this year.
8 03:19 Siyabonga’s friend I started hearing about Mercedes in 2013. I have never heard about people dying from Mercedes before. When I took it before, nothing happened I was okay. But this (school) term I wasn’t okay. Your entire body locks up and you hallucinate. And you lose your mind.
9 03:50 Claire to camera in hospital Claire: Over the last 2 month Dr Roshan Maharaja has seen over 40 patience’s that have been admitted here at King Dininzulu hospital after taking Mercedes
10 03:58 Claire interviews Dr. Roshan Claire: What is it exactly that is making Mercedes fatal?
Dr: From the history given by patience Mercedes has similar effects to extacsy what was different it that it was prolonged. Where is extascy lasts up to 6 hours in your system, Mercedes lasting 12-24 hours and we ae=re seeing side effects up to 48 hours of injection of a single tablet.
Claire: and what symtems where those patiences displaying?
DR: Patience where presentiung with extreme aggitation and restlessness, they were having hallucinations some patience had abnormal muscle breakdown and had kidney injury
11 04:39 V/O in hospital V/O: This kidney failure is what caused the 10 Mercedes fatalities
12 04:43 Khanyi Khanyi: My brothers friend called my other brother called Sipho and told my brother can you please come done it seems like your brother is having a problem. And we go there and we saw Siyabonga lying down in the road standing on side of the road pavement and I did go there to him to feel what was really happen being I checked all the pulse and there was no pulse. No heart and he was freezing all over his body I just saw for myself that he is no more.
13 05:20 Siyabonga’s Friend Friend: When we got to the clinic, we asked about Siyabonga Mngadi. We saw him and he were covered with a white cloth. After seeing his body everything because sour. I miss him very much.

14 06:23 DR DR: Mercedes is a public health crisis we have already seen fatalities from it and we need to addresses it early to prevent further fatalities

15 06:36 SGT. Ngobese inter Ngobese: You can rest assured our crime intelligence, Hawks all other special units are underground because we want to get to the crust of the matter where does this drug called Mercedes come from?
16 06:51 Zodwa speaks about Siyabonga Zodwa: Siyabonga was a respectful child at home. I was supporting him and counting on him to finish school and make something of himself. Because one day when I pass away he can stay and be able to survive and live
17 07:208 Khanyi speaks about Siyabonga Khanyi: My dream for Siyabonga was seeing him growing together, growing old together
18 07:18 Zodwa Zodwa: I miss him he used to help… I cant talk anymore
19 07:26 V/O V/0: The source of Mercedes is still unknown by the SAPS and while it is so easily available on the streets of KwaZulu Natal more young people could die from this deadly drug
